collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: Nobody can make the old shiny black pots anymore, and a villager decides to try: keep experimenting, or give up gracefully.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A few pieces of very old pottery have been found in the gardens over the years: thin, hard and glossy black, so shiny you can see your face in them. Nobody on Isola can make pots like that anymore. Whoever knew how is long gone, and they didn't leave instructions. (subject) has decided to try. (friend) is helping.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They try different clays, hotter fires, smoke, burying the pots in leaves, polishing them with stones. The pots come out brown, grey, cracked, lumpy and, once, exploded. After a whole season, (subject) produces one that's dark grey and a little bit shiny. It's not the same. It's the closest anyone has come in generations. They put it next to the old pieces. It looks proud.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: After a month of failures, (subject) gives up. "Maybe some things are just gone," (subject.he/she) says. (friend) agrees. They keep the old pieces safe on a shelf in the meeting hut, with a note carved beside them: "Nobody knows how." Children come and look at their own faces in the shine. (subject) still wonders, sometimes, late at night, what the trick was.
